item.description: server : fix response_format json_schema when schema is not nested in the json_schema wrapper (#28697) * server : accept top-level schema in response_format with type json_schema The OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint only applied the schema when it was nested inside response_format.json_schema.schema. When the schema was provided directly as response_format.schema (as documented in the server README, and used by some clients), it was silently ignored and generation ran unconstrained. Also mention json_schema in the error message for invalid response_format types, document the OpenAI wrapper form in the README, and add a test case for the top-level schema form. Fixes #10732 * server : let the json_schema wrapper take precedence by presence Pick the schema source based on whether response_format has a json_schema key, instead of falling back when the parsed wrapper schema is empty. An empty schema {} is valid (any JSON value), so the old check let a top-level schema override an explicit {} in the wrapper. item.description: ggml : implement the backward pass for TRI (#30712) * ggml: implement the backward pass for TRI GGML_OP_TRI had no case in the backward switch, so a trainable graph containing it aborted with "unsupported ggml op for backward pass: TRI". The op is linear, so its gradient is masked the same way. The incoming gradient is not necessarily contiguous (the backward of a transpose hands over a view) and ggml_tri requires contiguity, so it is made contiguous first. test_tri gains a post_transpose variant (out = transpose(tri(a))) that aborts as above without this change. * ggml : simplify the TRI backward pass Pass the gradient directly to ggml_tri and drop the transpose test. item.description: ggml : update CUDA/Metal radix Top-K to make tied selections deterministic (#31084) * ggml : fix for the radix TOP_K thread timing bug * make the key an ordered 64-bit pair * a rewrite without shift-skip logic * fix casts * warp-contiguous layout * reduce the scope removing vulkan+metal changes * turn it off for Metal/ROCm, note about cub::DeviceTopK * fix the hip build * skip Vulkan as well * popc lambda from fattn * do block_cols math in int64_t * make it allowlist bc SYCL looks non deterministic too * ggml : make Metal radix Top-K tied selections deterministic The radix top-k kernel gathered the selected indices with atomic counters, so the order of the tied candidates at the threshold (and, with more ties than remaining slots, the subset itself) depended on the thread scheduling. Replace the two atomic compaction loops with a deterministic scheme: count the elements above and tied with the threshold in contiguous per-thread chunks, rank them with a simdgroup scan and a serial scan over the (now unused) radix histogram, and write each kept element exactly once in column order. The output is now byte-identical across runs. This is also faster than the atomic version: the strided atomic loops become contiguous passes, reducing top-k times by ~20-45% on M5 Ultra, with tie-heavy shapes within a few percent. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * tests : enable deterministic top-k check on Metal, add radix-path tie cases Metal now produces deterministic tied selections for the radix top-k path, so the determinism self-check runs for the MTL backend as well. Add eval cases covering the radix path (ncols > 2048) with more ties at the threshold than remaining slots, and tie-heavy perf cases to monitor the cost of the deterministic tie handling. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * ggml : use coalesced accesses in the Metal radix Top-K compaction The deterministic compaction walked contiguous per-thread chunks with scalar sequential loads, which the memory system of the M2 Ultra can not overlap well: the radix Top-K times regressed by ~1.5-2.4x on the large-ncols shapes. Give each warp a contiguous chunk of the row instead and let the lanes interleave within it with stride 32, so every access is fully coalesced. The lanes write their kept elements at lane-major ranks, which is deterministic, and only a tie overflow falls back to a per-step cross-lane ranking to keep the lowest tied indices in column order. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * tests : remove the extra top-k tie and perf cases The radix-path eval and tie-heavy perf cases were added to validate and benchmark the Metal deterministic tie handling. Keep only the enabling of the determinism self-check for the MTL backend. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * metal: scan the radix bins and warp totals with a simdgroup The radix top-k selected the threshold bucket with a serial scan of the 256 bins by thread 0 in each of the 4 passes, and ranked the warps of the compaction with two serial scans by thread 0. The first simdgroup now does both: each lane sums 8 bins, an exclusive prefix sum and a ballot find the lane that reaches the k-th value, and the warp totals get their exclusive bases from simd_prefix_exclusive_sum. * tests: enable the deterministic top-k check on ROCm HIP has no cub::DeviceTopK, so every row goes through the radix or bitonic path, which break ties in the same way in each run. The check covers all tie cases on ROCm, including the 1 and 2 row ones that CUDA skips. * cuda: remove the redundant radix top-k counter reset Address review from ORippler. top_k_radix_init already zeroes greater_count for each chunk of rows and top_k_radix_select keeps it, so the reset kernel before the gather is one launch with no effect. --------- Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu 24.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.5 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: ggml-cuda : add d_state=64 fast path to SSM_SCAN kernel (#31818) Zamba2 and similar architectures use a state size of 64 in their recurrent-scan step, which fell outside the GPU kernel's existing fast paths (96, 128, 256). Every scan step was falling back to CPU, bottlenecking generation to 6-7 tok/s against the 50-70 tok/s band other architectures achieve on the same hardware. Add a 4th template instantiation for d_state=64, following the existing pattern; no change to the underlying math. Verified against the existing CPU-reference correctness harness with 3 new test cases built from Zamba2's real hyperparameters (28/28 passing). Measured ~35% throughput improvement (11 -> 15.1 tok/s) on Zamba2-7B- Instruct. Full parity with other architectures not yet reached - a separate, unrelated fraction of scan calls (~28%) still falls back to CPU for a cause not yet diagnosed. item.description: llama_moe_cache: run missed experts on CPU, add tuning script (#30966) * moe-cache : compute part of the misses on the CPU --moe-cache-cpu-share F computes a share F of the MoE cache misses on the CPU from the host experts instead of uploading them. The graph builds the expert FFN twice: on the device from the cache slots, where the misses left to the CPU read zero slots, and on the CPU from the host experts, where the experts computed on the device have id -1. The two results are added before the down bias. - ggml-cpu: MUL_MAT_ID skips negative ids and writes zero rows - sched: the copy callback is called for all the inputs of a split, and before the host sync when there are no events - the slot lookup callback reads the inputs of the CPU part together with the selected experts, so the CPU part does not wait for the device, and its result is copied back asynchronously - each token uses distinct zero slots, mul_mat_id does not support an expert selected twice by a token - LLAMA_MOE_CACHE_TRACE writes the selected experts of each lookup, for a simulator of the cache * scripts : add moe-cache-tune.py to pick the MoE cache arguments The script wraps a llama-server command: it starts the server at two cache sizes and three CPU shares, fits the upload and CPU speeds of the machine, and replays the routing of the runs through a copy of the cache logic to predict other sizes and shares. It prints the recommended --moe-cache-mib and --moe-cache-cpu-share. docs/moe-cache.md describes the MoE cache arguments and the script. * add am17an as codeowner for MoE cache * moe-cache : upload all the misses until the cache is full With a high --moe-cache-cpu-share, few misses are uploaded, so an empty cache fills slowly and more misses than needed go to the CPU. The CPU share now starts once all the slots of a cache group hold an expert. moe-cache-tune.py replays the same rule. * add backend sync for async transfer queue * moe-cache : let the scheduler copy the results of the CPU part * Fix MSVC compilation * remove sync change * llama-graph : extract the CPU share condition into can_cpu_share * llama-graph : make llm_graph_params::moe_cache const The graph construction no longer updates the MoE cache directly: the CPU parts of the layers are accumulated in the graph result and applied to the cache in llama_context::process_ubatch, after the graph inputs are set and before the graph is computed. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB) * scripts : replay the ClassLRU policy in moe-cache-tune.py * moe-cache : pick CPU misses by CRF instead of random (#31853) * moe-cache : remove the backend logic of the CPU part from the graph The CPU part reads the host experts, so the scheduler places it on the CPU without set_tensor_backend. The cache gives no CPU map for batches that a device would offload. Graphs with a CPU part look up their own slot map, so the graph does not register the part with the cache. ggml-backend : the inputs of the next split that are already computed are copied to host memory before the current split runs, so a CPU split does not wait for the device split before it. item.description: metal : fix GROUP_NORM for ne03 > 1 and non-contiguous inputs (#31852) The kernel_group_norm_f32 kernel and its host dispatch ignored the batch dimension (ne03) of the source tensor: only ngrp threadgroups were dispatched and each normalized the flat range [tgpig*gs, (tgpig+1)*gs) with gs = ne00*ne01*ceil(ne02/ngrp). For tensors with ne03 > 1, all but the first ne00*ne01*ne02 elements were left unwritten (exposed by the new GROUP_NORM test with ne=[3,1,1,65537], num_groups=1). Dispatch one threadgroup per (group, i03) pair (ngrp in x, ne03 in z, same work distribution as the Vulkan backend) and compute per-batch statistics, matching the CPU reference. Also clamp the group element count for the last group when ne02 is not divisible by ngrp and use int64_t indexing. The kernel now only requires ggml_is_contiguous_rows(op->src[0]) instead of full contiguity: it addresses src0 and dst with their own strides (nb03 and the dst strides are added to the kernel args - dst can be a strided view of src0 with ggml_group_norm_inplace) and falls back from the flat fast path to a strided path that decodes the linear element index when rows or channels are padded. The flat/strided selection is done on the host in ggml_metal_library_get_pipeline_group_norm and compiled into one of two specialized pipeline variants via a FC_group_norm_flat function constant, so the dead path is eliminated at pipeline creation. GROUP_NORM support is also gated on F32 src and dst in supports_op - the kernel only implements f32 and an f16 input would silently be read as f32. item.description: server: visit parent slots before child slots (#30779) * server: visit parent slots before child slots A parent slot wakes its waiting child slots once it finishes the shared prompt prefix, while slots are visited in id order. When a child task lands on a lower slot id than its parent, the child is visited before the parent wakes it and waits an extra batch to process its suffix. Non-child slots are now visited before active child slots, so every child woken by its parent joins the same batch. * server: check systemone test events through test tags The systemone tests matched free-form debug messages, including the formatted f_keep value of the prompt cache. item.description: model: add Kimi-K3.1-Pro text model (#31779) * model: add Kimi-K3.1-Pro text model K3 with the full-attention MLA layers replaced by DSA: on this checkpoint 24 of the 93 layers carry a lightning indexer (32 heads x 128, top_k 2048, no rope). The KDA (linear-attention) layers and the rest of the K3 skeleton - cross-layer residuals, latent MoE, situ, MLA output gate, full-rank KDA gate - are unchanged, so this reuses the K3 graph and converter and adds the indexer. Indexer: - the selection is an additive mask over the whole cache, not a gather of the top-k rows, so it reuses the existing sparse flash attention path; off that path the mask stays correct but still costs a kq over the cache - the indexer key LayerNorm takes its eps from the model's rms_norm_eps, because dsa_config declares no eps of its own Graph and cache: - new arch with four indexer tensors per DSA layer, and a hybrid memory that keeps a K-only MLA cache for those layers, recurrent state for the KDA layers, and the indexer key cache - the graph node budget shares the K3 entry Conversion: - KimiK31Model(KimiK3Model), picked by KimiK31ForConditionalGeneration - dsa_config becomes attention.indexer.{head_count,key_length,top_k,types} plus the indexer LayerNorm eps; the layer list is 1-indexed like linear_attn_config's, and the converter asserts that it covers exactly the full-attention layers - the routed experts stay MXFP4 and are repacked as in K3, not dequantized - the vision tower and mm_projector are skipped: text only for now - the arch key follows the checkpoint's own model_type ("kimi_k31") and the loader registers KimiK31ForConditionalGeneration; the release name carries a -Pro suffix that nothing in the config or the tensor names uses Quantisation: the indexer's q_b, k and proj are kept out of the quant overrides, since the top-k selection is sensitive to their precision. Verified on an 8-layer slice against the HF checkpoint: 38 tensors checked exactly, the indexer metadata against the config, and the selection against full attention - identical PPL at top_k beyond the context length, divergent once top_k is forced below it. item.description: hexagon: conv_2d optimizations and support for conv_3d (#31814) * hexagon: Generalization of CONV_2D implementation for CONV_3D - New op HTP_OP_CONV_3D is wired through htp-ops.h, main.c (shares op_conv_2d) and the op remap in htp-kparams.cpp. - conv_3d runs on the existing HMX tiled (implicit GEMM) conv2d path. Only the input stage unfolds depth. - 256-entry DMA queue can no longer overflow Assisted-by: Claude Code * hexagon: modify checking to eliminate divide-by-zero hazards * hexagon: conv2d tiled: compute the conv_3d unfold divisors on the host The KH and OH fastdiv values used to unfold conv_3d kh into (kd, kh) and oh into (od, oh) were built per op on the device, each with a 64-bit divide. Pass them in the kernel params instead; they fit in the space the window variant already reserves, so the struct size does not change. item.description: tests : qualify isnan and signbit with std:: (#31791) * tests : qualify isnan and signbit with std:: The unqualified calls rely on the C math.h names also being present in the global namespace, which is not the case for the NetBSD 11.99.9/x86_64 gcc 14.4.0 build reported in the issue. Prefix the calls with std:: to select the standard C++ overloads declared by . ref: https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/issues/1681 Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : qualify C math calls with std:: Follow-up to the isnan / signbit fix: make the remaining math calls in test-quantize-fns.cpp consistent with the std:: isfinite / max / numeric_limits already used in the same file. The float variants are overloads in C++, not distinct names, so the mapping is fabsf -> std::fabs, copysignf -> std::copysign, nextafterf -> std::nextafter - not std::fabsf & friends, which do not exist in libstdc++ and would break the gcc build. NAN and INFINITY are macros and are left unqualified. Only behavioural difference: array_rmse() fed a double accumulator to sqrtf(), now std::sqrt() keeps the computation in double. The result is more accurate and differs from the previous value by at most 1.4e-7 relative, three orders of magnitude below the tightest tolerance in this test. item.description: vulkan: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (#29772) * vulkan: add F16 input to the FWHT The Vulkan FWHT accepts F32 input only. This adds an F16 source variant of the shader, for both the subgroup and the shared-memory paths, so the kernel reads an F16 source directly instead of requiring a converted copy. The F16 shader needs shader-float16, so the pipelines are only created when the device reports it. A null pipeline makes ggml_vk_can_use_fwht fall back, which is the same path an unsupported width already takes. supports_op and the dispatch both already route through ggml_vk_can_use_fwht, so there is a single place asking whether an op qualifies; nothing to consolidate here the way the CUDA/Metal ports needed. test-backend-ops on an M5 Pro (MoltenVK, fp16: 1): MUL_MAT 1128/1128, including all 24 Hadamard cases (18 existing F32, 6 new F16). Assisted-by: Codex * vulkan: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 The Vulkan FWHT covers block widths 64 to 512; wider blocks fall back to the dense matmul. Extend the width list to 8192 and pick the shader per width: the subgroup shader keeps n/subgroup_size values per invocation, so widths above 512 (or a subgroup narrow enough to exceed 64 values per invocation) use the shared-memory shader with one row per workgroup and a 256-wide block. The rows per workgroup become a specialization constant so the dispatch matches. Pipelines for a width are only created when the device's shared-memory and workgroup-invocation limits allow it; otherwise that width keeps the fallback. This is the Vulkan counterpart to #29100 (CUDA). Stacked on #29101; the last commit is the one to review. item.description: tests: fix CI flakes of TOPK_MOE caused by near ties (#31426) * tests: fix CI flakes of TOPK_MOE caused by near ties With uniform random logits, two experts sometimes land within one f32 ulp of each other at a routing boundary, mostly with sqrt_softplus gating whose output range is narrow. A backend whose gating differs by a few ulps from the CPU then picks the other expert and the test fails. Draw each row of logits again until the group selection and the final top-k both have a relative margin of 1e-4, computed on the host in double precision. * tests: build the TOPK_MOE logits by inverting the gating function Draw the selection scores (probs plus bias) of each row as a random permutation of a grid, move the experts of the best groups up by half a step, and set the logits to the inverse of the gating function at these scores. Every expert and group decision is then one grid step apart on all backends, and the host no longer recomputes the routing. item.description: ## Overview This release adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization support, a new flash_attn_ext_rows op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. Four new architectures are supported (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4), audio generation and transcription expand with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, and the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models get major prefill optimizations. ggml is updated to v0.29.0, bringing FP8 E4M3, flash attention rows, NCCL-based multi-node tensor parallelism and performance work across the CPU, CUDA, SYCL, Metal, Vulkan, OpenCL and Hexagon backends. The server and UI receive a round of fixes and refinements. ### Highlights - Quant: OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type (saturating mode) with conversion helpers and a new ftype (#27512) - llama: flash_attn_ext_rows - more efficient unified KV for multi-seq, restoring non-unified KV prefill performance (#29510) - ggml: batched tensor copy API (ggml_backend_tensor_copy_n/set_n/get_n) superseding the _2d API, implemented for Metal and CUDA (#30881) - For a 3rd year in a row, llama.cpp is a featured repo in the Github Octoverse report: ### API changes - llama.h: add LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_F8_E4M3 (#27512) - mtmd.h: add MTMD_GEN_AUDIO_TYPE_CHATTERBOX and n_voices to mtmd_gen_audio_info (#30993) - mtmd.h: add predefined-voice APIs: mtmd_gen_audio_voice_name(), mtmd_gen_audio_get_voice(), mtmd_gen_state_set_ref() (#30993) - mtmd.h: add mtmd_bitmap_is_voice() and mtmd_gen_audio_read_tensor() (#30993) - mtmd.h: add MTMD_VIDEO_TEMPLATE_QWEN3VL video prompt template (#31619) - server: GET /props reports the model's predefined TTS voices; the TTS endpoint accepts predefined voice names (#30993) - server: /v1/responses now merges extra_params (seed, min_p, ...) into the converted chat-completions response (#30959) ### New models - Clover-35B-A3B-Preview diffusion model, AR mode (#31306) - Limite 1B - Violetto (#29433) - Metis-1.6 (Praxis ~2.9B and Logos ~10.2B): hybrid Mamba-2 / GQA attention with fixed-depth recurrence and LatentMoE (#31134) - Mistral Large 4 (#31376) ### Core changes - gemma4: graph optimizations with massive prefill gains for E2B and E4B (#31356); create token_embd before the tied output in gemma3n and gemma4 (#31394) - LFM3: enable NVFP4 GGUFs (#31608), enable tensor split (#31431), quantize the audio codec decoder (#31386) - spec dec: save and restore MTP hidden state in context checkpoints (#30141) and record LFM3 layer inputs (#31598) - dflash: copy hidden features via device copies (#31506); qwen4exp: write the conv state tail without an intermediate cont (#31443) - model loading: reuse the tensor staging buffer and skip the direct-IO bounce buffer (#31321) - kv-cache: keep Hadamard rotation constants on the GPU (#31073) and fix attention tensor rotation in layers with shared KV (#31406) - kv-cache: never return 0 kv_rows for sequences without cells (#31570) and refuse rollbacks past the snapshots of the last ubatch (#31368) - Gemma4 MTP assistant: follow ctx_other devices and flash-attention setting (#31635); DSV4: remove simple batch splitting (#31300) - chat: strip the qwen3-coder think block with reasoning_format none (#31380) and end reasoning budget forcing on a prompt end tag (#31374) - chat: allow a constraint type after the gpt-oss final channel (#31556); common: fix -hf tag matching inside longer quant names (#31620) and bound control vector layer indices (#31336) - tools: reject mismatched shards in GGUF split merge (#31579), fix imatrix --nextn crash (#31522), fix gguf-py np_roundf dropping the sign (#31310) - vendor: miniaudio 0.11.26 (#31459) and cpp-httplib 0.64.0 (#31400); embed an app manifest in all Windows executables (#31329) ### Multi-modality changes - add Chatterbox TTS support (#30993) - add Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe support: offline transcription in 40 languages with prompt context and speaker attribution (#31471) - Pocket TTS: support predefined voices without voice cloning (#31429) - accurate support for the qwen3-vl video prompt format (#31619) - resize Gemma 4 images without letterbox padding (#30922) and fix InternVL CLS token order (#30886) ### Server changes - cap shared decision prefixes at the first output (#30710) - restore the speculative checkpoint for drafts longer than n_rs_seq (#31350) ### UI changes - add MCP group checkboxes in the tools settings (#31303) and request persistent storage on startup (#31299) - keep chats at the bottom until the reader scrolls up (#31311) and show the submit button when the input has content (#31324) - reveal the collapsed sidebar from its logo (#31307) and align alert dialog styling (#31312) - keep queued steering messages in their own conversation (#31304) and show an interrupted state for tool calls that never returned (#31314) - disable model deletion the server would refuse (#31305) and prefer a loading model in pre-selection (#31326) - add a Playwright harness for recording demo videos (#31318) and run local browser tests in installed Chrome (#31596) ### ggml changes - v0.29.0: ggml v0.29.0 adds an OCP FP8 E4M3 tensor type, a new ggml_flash_attn_ext_rows op where each query slice attends to its own list of K/V rows, a batched tensor copy API, and initial support for multi-node tensor parallelism through a new multi-process communicator interface. Core improvements include bounding tensor views by the bytes their strides reach, zero-copy GGUF export of host-buffer tensors, and vm_allocate-based allocations on Apple platforms. Performance work spans all major backends: new SVE kernels in the CPU backend, DPAS flash attention for quantized KV in SYCL, fused MoE MMQ in CUDA, faster MXFP4 mat-vec in Metal, split-K tuning in Vulkan, and a large expansion of quantized GEMM/GEMV coverage in OpenCL. item.description: ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach (#31584) * ggml: bound views by the bytes their strides reach A view was checked against its source with the size of a contiguous tensor of the same shape, computed before its strides were set. Views whose rows overlap failed that check although they stay inside their source, and views with wider strides passed it while reaching past the end. The view functions now pass their strides to the tensor constructor, which checks the bytes they actually reach, like ggml_nbytes. The conv windows of delta_net are created with all their rows at once instead of being widened after the check. * ggml: assert that a strided view starts from contiguous elements The view functions set nb[0] to the type size, so the source must have contiguous elements along dim 0 for the view to read them. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) - macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) DISABLED - macOS Intel (x64) - iOS XCFramework **Linux:** - Ubuntu x64 (CPU) - Ubuntu arm64 (CPU) - Ubuntu s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (CPU) - Ubuntu 26.04 s390x (zDNN) - Ubuntu x64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu arm64 (Vulkan) - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.8 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 libraries - Ubuntu x64 (ROCm 10.0) - Ubuntu x64 (OpenVINO) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP32) - Ubuntu x64 (SYCL FP16) - Linux arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Android:** - Android arm64 (CPU) - Android arm64 (Snapdragon: CPU, Adreno GPU, Hexagon NPU) - setup guide **Windows:** - Windows x64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (CPU) - Windows arm64 (OpenCL Adreno) - Windows x64 (CUDA 12) - CUDA 12.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows arm64 (CUDA 13) - CUDA 13.4 DLLs - Windows x64 (Vulkan) - Windows arm64 (Vulkan) - Windows x64 (OpenVINO) - Windows x64 (SYCL) - Windows x64 (ROCm 10.0) **openEuler:** - DISABLED - openEuler x86 (310p) - openEuler x86 (910b, ACL Graph) - openEuler aarch64 (310p) - openEuler aarch64 (910b, ACL Graph) **UI:** - UI

item.description: vulkan: fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup (#31079) * vulkan : fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup On the non-OCP path, ue4m3_fp32_lut has 128 entries and is indexed with the raw scale byte. ggml_validate_row_data accepts every byte and ggml_ue4m3_to_fp32 ignores bit 7, so a byte >= 0x80 reads past the shared array. Vulkan robustness does not cover shared memory. Size the table, both init loops, and the two host shared-memory budgets to 256 entries. ue4m3_to_fp32_build() already masks the exponent and treats only 0 and 0x7F as special, so entries 128-255 match the CPU. A 256-entry table keeps 0xFF distinct from 0x7F: the CPU decodes 0xFF as a non-zero value and 0x7F as zero. Each NVFP4 pipeline uses 512 more bytes of shared memory. ggml_fp32_to_ue4m3 never sets bit 7, so models quantized by llama.cpp are unaffected.
